subject: Can't redeploy app, appDependencies() finds dependencies on local packages which should be there

messages.author: 5580959ea4d79ad5
messages.subject: Can't redeploy app, appDependencies() finds dependencies on local packages which should be there
parts:
Dear all,

yesterday, I deployed succesfully an app to shinyapps.io.

This morning, deploy doesn't work any longer because of the following error message:

Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading application bundle...Error: 
* Unable to deploy package dependency 'Colibri'
  
  The package was installed locally from source. Only packages
  installed from CRAN, BioConductor and GitHub are supported.

* Unable to deploy package dependency 'season'
  
  The package was installed locally from source. Only packages
  installed from CRAN, BioConductor and GitHub are supported.
Execution halted

As I am aware that apps using locally installed packages I have removed such dependendencies from the sources as can be shown by output of a grep:

system("grep -E 'library|require' *.R", intern = TRUE)

## [5] "server.R:library(RJDBC)"      "server.R:library(stringr)"   
## [7] "ui.R:library(shiny)"

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: Can't redeploy app, appDependencies() finds dependencies on local packages which should be there
parts:
Uwe,

It is very unlikely that shinyapps is looking elsewhere. 
What do you get for "getwd()" command?
What changed in your code between yesterday and today?
Can you try restarting R session (from RStudio menu) and then run "shinyapps::appDependencies()" command again? Doubt that this would change anything, but worth trying.
Do you mind sharing your code with us to take a closer look?

Fereshteh

messages.author: 5580959ea4d79ad5
messages.subject: Re: Can't redeploy app, appDependencies() finds dependencies on local packages which should be there
parts:
Dear all,

I inspected my code more carefully and found another dependency to a private package in the form <package>::<function>.
After removing this dependency, the app was successfuly deployed.

So appDependency() was right and I ignored it. How embarrassing!

Thank you for your attention,
Uwe
